answer.evidence: The sign is drawn flat-on as a vertical panel. The header at rows 1-5 is a front-facing strip (width 14, then 16 at rows 2-4, then 14). Row 6 is only a dark outline row, not a front-edge line, and no eave shadow follows it. The white oval inside the header is a label, not an ellipse top. The blue panel (rows 7-26) is lettering on a vertical face. Rows 27-31 are a dark base. No horizontal surface is visible, so the main top is 0 rows and the front face is about 25 rows. This matches the red 'front elevation' references, not the green ones.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical sign with a dark navy body, a lighter blue panel and white text. It has 10 visible tones per tile, against 6 for bus-shelter, 12 for kiosk and 20 for vending. That is above the bus shelter, a little below the kiosk and well below the vending machine. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the surface has no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark blue, as in the references, not a sticker-style black line. Shading on the body has about 4 steps (edge, dark, mid, highlight rim) against 5-6 on the vending machine. The piece is small and simple, and it sits within the range of the shipped modern_city references. It looks slightly flatter than vending-a, but it is accepted as comparable to kiosk-a and bus-shelter-a.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical signboard in a dark navy body with a pale lettered panel. Measured facts: 10 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12 is slightly higher), but below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, matching kiosk-a and vending-a and better than bus-shelter-a (9%). The sign face shows lettering and a frame, which gives some texture, though there is little grain on the body. It is a thin, sparse prop, and by eye it sits comfortably between bus-shelter-a and vending-a without looking flatter or more sticker-like than the shipped references. A careful artist would accept it next to them.
